title: Flyback Converter (isolated)
summary: Galvanically isolated single-switch converter; an inverting buck-boost with a coupled inductor (transformer). In continuous conduction the output equals the input scaled by n * D / (1 - D), where n = N2/N1 is the turns ratio.

ports.name: in
ports.description: Positive primary-side input supply rail feeding the primary winding and switch.

ports.name: sw
ports.description: Primary switching node between the primary winding and the low-side switch.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Isolated regulated output rail across the secondary rectifier, filter capacitor, and load.

ports.name: sec_gnd
ports.description: Secondary-side ground reference (output return), galvanically isolated from pri_gnd.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive command for the primary switch from the controller.

parameters.name: L1
parameters.description: Primary-side magnetizing inductance (the flyback stores energy here; L2 = n**2 * L1 is the inductance seen from the secondary).

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Turns ratio n = N2/N1 (secondary turns over primary turns).

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of the primary switch.

parameters.name: R_load
parameters.description: Load resistance seen at the output (R_load = Vout / Iout).

parameters.name: r_C
parameters.description: Output capacitor equivalent series resistance (ESR); sets the high-frequency zero.

design_equations.name: turns_ratio
design_equations.description: Turns ratio definition (Alonso eq. 4.5) and the relationship between primary and secondary magnetizing inductances (eq. 4.6).

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio
design_equations.description: Ideal CCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 4.12); the turns ratio n scales the buck-boost ratio D/(1-D).

design_equations.name: secondary_inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average secondary magnetizing current equals the DC output current (Alonso eq. 4.13).

design_equations.name: switch_average_current
design_equations.expression: I_S = I_L1 = n * D / (1 - D) * Iout
design_equations.description: Average primary (switch) current (Alonso eq. 4.14).

design_equations.name: magnetizing_current
design_equations.expression: I_M1 = I_L1 + n * I_L2 = n * Iout / (1 - D)
design_equations.description: Average magnetizing current referred to the primary (Alonso eq. 4.15).

design_equations.name: primary_inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak primary inductor current ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 4.49).

design_equations.name: secondary_inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak secondary inductor current ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 4.50), with L2 = n**2 * L1.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 4.51); the capacitor alone supplies the load during the on-time. ESR adds r_C times the diode current step.

design_equations.name: switch_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak blocking voltage across the primary switch (Alonso summary); a real device must also withstand the leakage-inductance spike, so a snubber/clamp is required on top of this.

design_equations.name: diode_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak reverse voltage across the secondary rectifier (Alonso summary).

design_equations.name: diode_peak_current
design_equations.description: Peak secondary (rectifier) current in CCM (Alonso summary); the primary switch peak is n*Iout/(1-D) + dI_L1/2.

design_equations.name: boundary_load_resistance
design_equations.description: CCM-DCM boundary load resistance (Alonso eq. 4.53): CCM when R_load < R_lim, DCM when R_load > R_lim.

design_equations.name: boundary_output_current
design_equations.expression: Io_lim = Vout * (1 - D)**2 / (2 * n**2 * L1 * fsw)
design_equations.description: Output current at the CCM-DCM boundary (Alonso eq. 4.52).

design_equations.name: dcm_conversion_ratio
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = D / sqrt(k),  k = 2 * L1 * fsw / R_load
design_equations.description: DCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 4.63-4.64); load-dependent and, notably, independent of the turns ratio n because all stored energy is delivered each cycle (only the primary inductance L1 appears).

design_equations.name: dcm_output_ripple
design_equations.expression: dVout = n**2 * L1 * (D * Vin / (n * L1 * fsw) - Vout / R_load)**2 / (2 * Vout * C)
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in DCM (Alonso eq. 4.72).

design_equations.name: rhp_zero
design_equations.expression: f_rhpz = (1 - D)**2 * R_load / (2 * pi * D * n**2 * L1)
design_equations.description: Right-half-plane zero frequency of Gd(s) (zero at s = (1-D)**2 * R_load / (D * n**2 * L1) = (1-D)**2 * R_load / (D * L2)); it adds gain while subtracting phase, so it caps the achievable loop bandwidth.

design_equations.name: ccm_characteristic_polynomial
design_equations.description: Shared CCM denominator of every small-signal transfer function below; identical to the buck-boost denominator with the inductance replaced by the secondary-referred L2 = n**2 * L1.

design_equations.name: control_to_output_tf_ccm
design_equations.expression: Gd(s) = Vout(s)/d(s) = Vout*R_load*((1 - D)/D)*(1 - (D*n**2*L1/((1 - D)**2*R_load))*s)*(1 + r_C*C*s) / Den(s)
design_equations.description: Control-to-output transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 4.29); the flyback behaves dynamically as a buck-boost whose inductance is the secondary-referred L2 = n**2 * L1, including the right-half-plane zero factor and the ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C).

design_equations.name: audio_susceptibility_tf_ccm
design_equations.expression: Gb(s) = Vout(s)/Vin(s) = n*R_load*D*(1 - D)*(1 + r_C*C*s) / Den(s)
design_equations.description: Input-to-output (audio susceptibility) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 4.35); n times the buck-boost result (turns-ratio coupling), with no right-half-plane zero.

design_equations.name: output_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop output impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 4.46); the buck-boost result with inductance n**2 * L1, with Zo(0) = 0 and Zo(inf) approx r_C.

design_equations.name: input_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop input impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 4.38); 1/n**2 times the buck-boost input impedance, with Zi(0) = (1 - D)**2*R_load/(n**2*D**2) and Zi(inf) -> infinity.

control_notes: The flyback is an inverting buck-boost wrapped around a coupled inductor (transformer), so its small-signal behaviour maps directly onto the buck-boost. In CCM it is a buck-boost whose inductance is the secondary-referred value L2 = n**2 * L1: every transfer function shares the denominator Den(s) above, and Gd(s) carries a right-half-plane (RHP) zero at f_rhpz = (1-D)**2*R_load/(2*pi*D*n**2*L1) whose frequency drops with load and duty cycle - keep the voltage-loop crossover well below it. The input-to-output and input-impedance transfer functions pick up the turns ratio (Gb is n times, Zi is 1/n**2 times the buck-boost result). In DCM (when R_load > R_lim = 2*n**2*L1*fsw/(1-D)**2) the plant collapses to first order, the RHP zero moves to very high frequency, and the DC gain becomes independent of n because only the primary inductance L1 governs energy transfer. Current-mode control is the usual choice. Practical isolated-design notes the ideal model omits: transformer leakage inductance causes a turn-off voltage spike on the switch (size an RCD clamp or snubber on top of the Vin + Vout/n rating), and feedback must cross the isolation barrier (optocoupler + shunt reference or an auxiliary/primary-side-regulation winding). All results follow from the averaged dependent-source model: the switch is replaced by its average current source and the diode by its average voltage source, then linearized about the DC operating point.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
